threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the market's a quick jaunt, not realizing you’ll need to navigate the endless queues and pop-up stalls for a good 45 minutes.
Caught a night bus from Brixton to Clapham, and there was a guy gleefully singing 'Wonderwall' while everyone pretended not to listen. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy in a full tuxedo casually waiting for the bus next to someone in pajamas. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you grab a döner, then stroll to a hidden courtyard where artists hang their creations on the walls, almost like a gallery.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they instinctively avoid the 24th St. BART entrance during rush hour like it's a wildfire zone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni at 9th and Market where a saxophonist played 'Take Five' while the bus was stuck behind a fire truck. Perfectly San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often miss that most locals don’t dine out until 9 PM. The evening buzz starts late, and the real vibe unfolds after sunset.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their confused look when the metro doors close just inches from their hand, still clutching a map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You always look confused when the 30 bus takes a detour down a side street; true locals just roll with it and pull out a book.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with Whitney Houston. Everyone just swayed, like we were in a weird late-night karaoke club.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I spotted a street musician playing an accordion next to a kebab shop at 3 AM, surrounded by a crowd singing along. That’s Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you see an entire street shut down for spontaneous dance parties after a BVG strike. Totally chaotic, yet perfectly Berlin.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they navigate the BART delays—immediate pivot to the 14 bus, not a second thought. Tourists just stand there, confused.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni up Jones yesterday; a guy started serenading us with an accordion. Didn’t even flinch when we passed the Civic Center chaos. Classic S.F.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the plaça and fancy bars, but the real vibe lives in the tiny streets, where locals chat and kids play.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still trying to navigate the metro map while clinging to a fresh cone of gelato at 10 PM.
